question: Which of the following rivers belongs to the Peninsular Plateau?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Krishna River** is one of the major rivers of the **Peninsular Plateau** in India.
 
• The Krishna River originates from the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The river is approximately **1,400 km long** and is the fourth-largest river in India in terms of water flow.
 
• The river supports agriculture and is a key source of irrigation for crops like rice, sugarcane, and cotton in the region.
 
• The Krishna River basin includes major dams such as the **Srisailam Dam** and **Nagarjuna Sagar Dam**, contributing to water management and hydroelectric power generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lohit River:**

 
 
• The Lohit River is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River and flows through the northeastern region of India, mainly in **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It originates from the eastern Himalayas in Tibet and is known for its swift currents.
 
• The Lohit River is not part of the Peninsular Plateau but is significant for the ecology and hydrology of the Brahmaputra basin.
 
 
 
• **Beas River:**
 
 
• The Beas River flows in the northern part of India, primarily in **Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.**
 
• It originates from the Himalayas near Rohtang Pass and is a tributary of the Indus River.
 
• Being part of the northern river system, it does not belong to the Peninsular Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Dibang River:**
 
 
• The Dibang River is another tributary of the Brahmaputra River and flows through Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It originates from the Mishmi Hills in the Himalayas and has a steep gradient with high water velocity.
 
• Since it belongs to the northeastern region, it does not form part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau Rivers:**
 
 
• Rivers originating in the Peninsular Plateau include **Godavari**, **Krishna**, **Kaveri**, and **Narmada.**
 
• These rivers are generally seasonal, depending significantly on monsoon rainfall.
 
• Unlike the northern Himalayan rivers, these rivers do not carry perennial snowmelt water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau:**

 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest landforms in India and consists of hard igneous and metamorphic rocks.
 
• It is characterized by flat-topped hills and valleys and is divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• Rivers originating from this plateau flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, except for rivers like Narmada and Tapi, which flow westward.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of India:**
 
 
• India has a diverse river system categorized into **Himalayan Rivers** and **Peninsular Rivers.**
 
• Himalayan rivers are snow-fed and perennial, while Peninsular rivers are rain-fed and seasonal.
